label: Town of Stowe
header:
# Town of Stowe municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 22; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 153 (Town of Stowe): sec. 401(a) lists the Moderator among the town's elected officers

Town of Stowe, 'Official Results - Annual Town and School Meeting, March 3, 2026', signed and certified by Penny A. Davis, Town Clerk (town website, Election Information & Results page): Article 1 (elect a Moderator for a one-year term) was decided by write-ins, and the signed official tally names 'Drew Clymer' with 75 votes, marked ELECTED in the tally's own legend (Leighton Detora received 20) -- a certified write-in outcome with the winner named in the official results (flagged on issue #163)

Town of Stowe, 2025 Annual Town Report, 'ELECTED TOWN OFFICERS' list (report p. 1, pre-dating the March 2026 election) and the March 3, 2026 annual meeting warning printed in the report: the report names Drew Clymer as Moderator on the one-year term expiring 2026, so the 2026 write-in result is his re-election

24 App. V.S.A. ch. 153 (Town of Stowe): sec. 401(a) lists only the Selectboard, the Moderator, and the Listers as the town's elected officers, and the charter's manager provisions (sec. 502 area) make the Town Clerk a manager-appointed officer

Town of Stowe official website: the 2025 Annual Town Report lists 'Town Clerk & Treasurer - Penny Davis' under Town Departments (staff), and Davis certifies the town's election results as Town Clerk, so she is seated APPOINTED
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): lists Penny Davis as Stowe's Town Clerk
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 153 (Town of Stowe): sec. 401(a) omits the Treasurer from the town's elected officers, and the charter's manager provisions make the Town Treasurer a manager-appointed officer
Town of Stowe official website: the 2025 Annual Town Report lists 'Town Clerk & Treasurer - Penny Davis' under Town Departments, so she is seated APPOINTED
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): lists Penny Davis as Stowe's Town Treasurer
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 153 (Town of Stowe): sec. 401(a) lists the Selectboard among the town's elected officers

Town of Stowe official website, Selectboard page ('Elected Officials'): Ethan Carlson, Chair (term expires 2027); Beth Gadbois, Vice Chair (2028); Paco Aumand (2029); Jo Sabel Courtney (2027); Nick Donza (2028)

Town of Stowe, 'Official Results - Annual Town and School Meeting, March 3, 2026', signed and certified by Penny A. Davis, Town Clerk (town website, Election Information & Results page): Francis 'Paco' Aumand was elected to the three-year seat with 623 votes and Nick Donza to the two-year seat with 626 votes

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): names Ethan Carlson (Chair), Francis 'Paco' Aumand, Jo Sabel Courtney, Nick Donza, and Beth Gadbois (Vice Chair)
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 153 (Town of Stowe): sec. 401(a) lists the Listers among the town's elected officers
Town of Stowe official website, Listers page ('Elected Officials'): Paul Percy, Chair; Adam Davis; Jeff Jackson

Town of Stowe, 'Official Results - Annual Town and School Meeting, March 3, 2026', signed and certified by Penny A. Davis, Town Clerk (town website, Election Information & Results page): Adam Davis was elected Lister for a three-year term with 651 votes; the town's Board of Listers minutes of June 3, 2026 record all three listers sworn and serving

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists twelve Stowe justices of the peace: Mary S. Black, Suzanne Clark, Leighton Detora, Lyndall Heyer, Liz Lackey, Charles Lusk, Maura Mancini, Marina Meerburg, Janet 'Jan' Reynolds, Pall Spera, Sarah Sterner, and Arnold Ziegel. The town's annual report and Board of Civil Authority page print the last name as 'Ziegler', but the listing's form is corroborated by his own email address in the listing and governs

jp_election.name: Town of Stowe Justice of the Peace Election 2024-11-05

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): the certified listing names twelve winners for Stowe's twelve justice of the peace seats. At the March 3, 2026 town meeting the voters adopted a floor article increasing the slate to fifteen for the next cycle; that change takes effect with the November 2026 election and does not alter the 2024 slate recorded here
